items.title: Trump invites battleground Republicans to Rose Garden dinner
items.standfirst: Many are hoping he will soon unleash his $400 million war chest to help save their majorities.
items.content: President Donald Trump has invited a group of GOP lawmakers including Republicans in competitive races to dine with him Wednesday night at the White House as many in the party press the president to unleash his massive war chest ahead of the November elections, according to five people with direct knowledge of the matter.They, like others, were granted anonymity to discuss private planning. Wisconsin Rep. Derrick Van Orden confirmed the event in a brief interview with POLITICO.“Of course,” Van Orden said when asked if he would go to the dinner.The White House plans to hold the dinner in the Rose Garden, according to two of the people who know about the invitation.Other House Republicans in tough races who were invited and plan to attend include Rep. Tom Barrett (R-Mich.) and Georgia Senate nominee Rep. Mike Collins, along with a wider group of GOP lawmakers.The White House invited at least several dozen lawmakers, according to two people familiar with the invitation list. The dinner also comes ahead of next week’s GOP midterm convention in Dallas, though attendance from Republican lawmakers is expected to be mixed. Barrett, for example, said in an interview Tuesday he is not planning to attend the convention and will instead campaign and spend time with his family. A White House spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Republicans are facing mounting electoral headwinds from the war in Iran, higher gas prices and new tariffs as they fight to hold onto their narrow congressional majorities in November.GOP incumbents are also eager for new infusions of resources to help dull Democrats’ attacks over voters’ cost-of-living concerns. Speaker Mike Johnson recently met with GOP megadonor Elon Musk, who has said he will spend millions to back the GOP again this cycle.Trump’s political operation, MAGA Inc., has used little of its $400 million war chest to support GOP lawmakers. But he recently helped boost Sen. Darline Graham over the line in her heated primary, with the group spending more than $800,000 on phone calls and texts for the political newcomer.Senate Republicans are eager for Trump to start spending for Ken Paxton in Texas as he has thus far been outspent on the airwaves by Democrat James Talarico and his allies.The scheduled dinner comes the same day Securing American Greatness, the nonprofit arm of Trump’s operation, is launching its first major ad buy of the general election.One ad features UFC President Dana White praising Trump along with a clip from Trump’s State of the Union address in February.Another ad touts the tax cuts passed through Republicans' domestic agenda bill last year, including “no tax on tips.” The ads are part of a nearly $1 million national TV reservation running over the next two weeks, per data tracking firm AdImpact.Both ads come as Trump advisers are reportedly planning to use his political organization to try and boost the president's approval ahead of the midterms.Erin Doherty, Aaron Pellish and Andrew Howard contributed reporting to this article.

items.title: Spain's Sanchez says no 'solid proof' that Morocco planned Ceuta crisis
items.standfirst: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has told lawmakers that there is no evidence the Ceuta migrant crisis was orchestrated by Morocco's government. His remarks come a day after tens of thousands of people took part in protests across the country to criticize his handling of the migrant influx. He acknowledged that Ceuta was both a humanitarian crisis and an administrative challenge. But he rejected the findings of a police report that seemed to lay blame on Morocco. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.
